youtube.title: Gillette's Viral Ad and the $8 Billion Hole That Opened Months Later
youtube.description:
In 2019 Gillette's 'We Believe' ad drew more than a million dislikes, and six months later its owner, Procter & Gamble, wrote the brand down by about $8 billion. Did one ad really cost Gillette that much?

This documentary follows the filings, not the outrage: the $57 billion purchase in 2005, the $1-a-month razor video in 2012, Gillette's slide from 71% to 54% of the US razor market, the 2017 price cut, and the reasons P&G itself gave for the write-down.

{CHAPTERS}

youtube.comment: Would you pay more for a Gillette razor today, or have you switched for good? 👇

sources.claim: On July 30, 2019, P&G wrote down Gillette by about $8 billion
sources.source: Procter & Gamble press release, fourth-quarter fiscal 2019 results, 30 July 2019

sources.claim: The charge was $8.3 billion before tax, about $8 billion after tax, non-cash, on Gillette Shave Care
sources.source: Procter & Gamble press release, 30 July 2019; P&G Form 10-K for fiscal 2019, filed August 2019

sources.claim: The charge turned P&G's quarter into a net loss of about $5.2 billion
sources.source: Procter & Gamble press release, fourth-quarter fiscal 2019 results, 30 July 2019; Reuters, 30 July 2019

sources.claim: P&G cited currency devaluations, a smaller blades and razors market as men shaved less, and increased competition
sources.source: Procter & Gamble press release, 30 July 2019; P&G Form 10-K fiscal 2019, goodwill and intangible assets note

sources.claim: P&G shares rose on the day of the write-down as sales beat expectations
sources.source: Reuters and The Wall Street Journal, 30 July 2019

sources.claim: The ad was released in January 2019 as 'We Believe: The Best Men Can Be'
sources.source: Gillette YouTube channel, posted 14 January 2019; BBC News, 15 January 2019

sources.claim: The ad passed a million YouTube dislikes within about a week; some viewers filmed themselves throwing razors away
sources.source: The Guardian and Forbes reporting, 15-22 January 2019

sources.claim: Nine days after release, P&G's finance chief said Gillette sales were 'in line with pre-ad levels'
sources.source: P&G fiscal Q2 2019 earnings call, 23 January 2019, as reported by Reuters, 23 January 2019

sources.claim: Gillette began in Boston in 1901; King C. Gillette patented the disposable safety razor blade
sources.source: Gillette company history; US Patent 775,134, granted 15 November 1904

sources.claim: Trac II twin-blade razor 1971, Mach3 1998, Fusion 2006, ProGlide with FlexBall 2014
sources.source: The New York Times launch coverage, 1971, 14 April 1998, 15 September 2005; P&G press release, April 2014

sources.claim: Gillette reported spending about $750 million developing the Mach3
sources.source: The New York Times, 15 April 1998

sources.claim: The slogan 'The Best a Man Can Get' first aired during the Super Bowl in January 1989
sources.source: Advertising Age, Gillette campaign history; BBC News, 15 January 2019

sources.claim: In January 2005 P&G agreed to buy Gillette for about $57 billion in stock, its largest acquisition
sources.source: P&G and Gillette joint announcement, 28 January 2005; The New York Times, 29 January 2005

sources.claim: Warren Buffett, whose Berkshire Hathaway was Gillette's largest shareholder, called it 'a dream deal'
sources.source: The New York Times and CNN Money, 28-29 January 2005

sources.claim: Berkshire Hathaway first invested in Gillette in 1989, buying $600 million of preferred stock
sources.source: Berkshire Hathaway annual shareholder letter, 1989

sources.claim: Gillette Stadium, home of the New England Patriots, has carried the Gillette name since 2002
sources.source: Kraft Group / Gillette naming announcement, August 2002

sources.claim: Gillette held 71% of the US men's razor market in 2010 and 54% in 2016
sources.source: Euromonitor International, as reported by The Wall Street Journal, 4 April 2017

sources.claim: Dollar Shave Club launched on 6 March 2012 with a video reported to cost about $4,500; 12,000 sign-ups in two days
sources.source: Inc. and Forbes, March 2012; company statements

sources.claim: Dollar Shave Club's entry plan cost $1 a month plus shipping
sources.source: Dollar Shave Club launch offer, March 2012, reported by Forbes, March 2012

sources.claim: Dollar Shave Club bought its blades from South Korea's Dorco
sources.source: The New York Times, 20 July 2016; Bloomberg, 2016

sources.claim: Harry's bought a German blade factory in Eisfeld in 2014 for about $100 million
sources.source: The New York Times, 21 January 2014

sources.claim: In December 2015 Gillette sued Dollar Shave Club alleging infringement of a blade-edge patent
sources.source: The Gillette Company v. Dollar Shave Club, US District Court for the District of Delaware, filed 17 December 2015

sources.claim: Gillette ran its own mail-order Shave Club
sources.source: Gillette Shave Club service, launched in the US 2015, reported by Advertising Age, 2015

sources.claim: Men were shaving less often, a change P&G named in its filings
sources.source: P&G Form 10-K fiscal 2019, Shave Care impairment discussion

sources.claim: Dollar Shave Club was reported to have over three million members in 2016
sources.source: The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times, 20 July 2016

sources.claim: In July 2016 Unilever agreed to buy Dollar Shave Club for about $1 billion
sources.source: Unilever press release, 20 July 2016; The New York Times, 20 July 2016

sources.claim: On 4 April 2017 Gillette cut US prices by up to 20%, about 12% on average, saying shoppers had told it prices were too high
sources.source: Gillette announcement, 4 April 2017; The Wall Street Journal, 4 April 2017

sources.claim: P&G Grooming net sales: FY2014 $8.0bn, FY2015 $7.4bn, FY2016 $6.8bn, FY2017 $6.6bn, FY2018 $6.6bn, FY2019 $6.2bn
sources.source: P&G Form 10-K annual reports, fiscal 2014-2019, segment results

sources.claim: Accounting rules require goodwill and brand values to be tested at least yearly and written down when impaired
sources.source: FASB Accounting Standards Codification 350, Intangibles: Goodwill and Other

sources.claim: Edgewell offered about $1.37 billion for Harry's in May 2019
sources.source: Edgewell Personal Care press release, 9 May 2019

sources.claim: In February 2020 the FTC sued to block the Edgewell-Harry's deal, arguing Harry's had pushed rivals including Gillette to cut prices; Edgewell walked away
sources.source: FTC press release and administrative complaint, 3 February 2020; Edgewell press release, 10 February 2020

sources.claim: Harry's razors sell in major US retail stores alongside Gillette
sources.source: Harry's and Target retail launch announcement, 2016

sources.claim: In 2023 Unilever sold a majority of Dollar Shave Club to an investment firm
sources.source: Unilever and Nexus Capital Management announcement, 3 October 2023

sources.claim: Intel declined to make the iPhone's chip
sources.source: Former Intel CEO interview, The Atlantic, 16 May 2013
